Being aggrieved by the order dated 14.10.2025 passed by the High Court of Punjab and Haryana at Chandigarh in CRM-50478 of 2024 in CRA-S-400 of 2023 by which the application filed by the appellant herein under Section 430 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 seeking suspension of sentence during the pendency of appeal was dismissed, the appellant is before this Court.

entities.text: High Court of Punjab and Haryana at Chandigarh
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Briefly stated the facts are that the appellant was convicted by the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Fast Track Special Court, Hoshiarpur and sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of ten years and to pay a fine of Rs.10,000/- under Section 376 of the Indian Penal Code,
1860 (for short, IPC) read with Section 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act,
2012 (for short,  POCSO Act) and in default of payment of fine to further undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of six months and to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of one year and to pay a fine of Rs.1,000/- under Section 506 IPC and in default of payment of fine to further undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of one month.

entities.label: COURT

entities.text:

sentences.text:
The said proceeding arose pursuant to FIR No.28 dated 06.03.2021 registered under Sections 376,
506, 120- B IPC and Section 6 of POCSO Act at Police Station- Sadar, Hoshiarpur.
Being aggrieved, the appellant preferred the aforesaid appeal along with an application for suspension of sentence which application was dismissed by the impugned order.
Hence, this appeal.
We have heard learned counsel for the appellant and learned counsel for the respondent(s)-State.
We have also perused the material on record.

Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that on conviction the sentence imposed upon the appellant is, inter alia, ten years of rigorous imprisonment; that the appellant had already undergone four years and eight months of actual sentence and more than five years of sentence with remission.
Further, the appellant has a good case on merits; that the hearing of the appeal by the High Court would inevitably be delayed since it is of the year 2023.

In the circumstances, this court Deepak @ Bansu vs State Of Punjab on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29520896/
1 may set aside the impugned order and grant suspension of sentence and bail by exercising powers under Section 389 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent(s)- State contended that the allegations against the appellant herein were serious and they have been proved and he has been convicted and hence, no indulgence may be shown to the appellant herein since the so-called victim was a minor at the time of the incident.
He, therefore, submitted that there is no merit in this appeal if at all the appellant could seek expeditious hearing of his appeal.
We have considered the arguments advanced at the bar.
We have also noted the fact that the appellant herein has already completed 50% of the sentence with remission and four years and eight months of actual incarceration.
The appeal is of the year 2023.
It is also noted that the appellant and the so-called victim have both been married to different persons.
Taking note of these circumstances, we find that the appellant is entitled to be released on suspension of his sentence by granting bail to him during the pendency of appeal before the High Court.

Consequently, the appellant shall be produced before the concerned trial court as early as possible and the appellant shall be released on bail subject to the terms and conditions to be imposed by the trial court.
However, the appellant shall appear before the High Court in case a direction is issued by the High Court for his presence before the High Court.
The appeal is allowed in the aforesaid terms.

,J.
(B.V. NAGARATHNA) ,J.
(K.V. VISWANATHAN) NEW DELHI;
